questions.q: One user reports they cannot see a journal that everyone else on the team can see. What does that pattern usually point to?
options: A corrupted journal batch that needs to be deleted
A security or role assignment issue, not a data problem
A period close issue affecting the whole ledger
An interface table error
questions.explain: When one person is missing access that everyone else has, the cause is almost always security or role assignment rather than the underlying data.

questions.q: Where would you look first to find out why a specific invoice is blocked from payment?
options: GL_INTERFACE
The Accounting Event Diagnostic report
The customer's statement
The Holds or Review tab on the invoice
questions.explain: Holds and Review tabs in Payables show exactly which rule placed a hold on a specific transaction.

questions.q: A background program like Journal Import or AutoInvoice completed, but some rows didn't load. What's the best source of evidence for which rows failed and why?
options: The relevant interface/error table and the process log
The user's description of the problem
The supplier setup page
The chart of accounts
questions.explain: Interface and error tables (like RA_INTERFACE_ERRORS_ALL or GL_INTERFACE) along with the process log identify exactly which rows were rejected and why.

questions.q: According to this lesson, what should you do before applying a fix you believe is correct?
options: Apply the fix immediately to save time
Skip confirmation if the ticket is high severity
Confirm the theory against the data, such as checking the full log or one more similar record
Ask the end user to confirm it instead of checking yourself
questions.explain: Confirming the theory first — by checking the data or log in more detail — costs a few minutes, while fixing the wrong thing in a financial system can require a documented correction.

questions.q: Which situation best illustrates 'what actually changed recently' as a likely root cause?
options: A report that has always shown the same format
A process that worked fine for months and suddenly fails the month after a new segment value was added
A field that has been blank since go-live
A user who has never had access to a business unit
questions.explain: Tickets are disproportionately caused by something new — a setup change, new value, or recent patch — rather than by existing behavior suddenly changing on its own.
